P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Partly established. The Bank of South Sudan's Circular No. 02/2025 requires written declaration of cash above USD 10,000 at borders and central-bank approval for institutions moving more than USD 50,000. Press reports describe restrictions on domestic US-dollar use. Rules for residents receiving foreign service income were not found.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Single press source captured; Bank of South Sudan circulars not captured on 2026-10-22; The EastAfrican (403).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Not established. Press reports indicate restrictions on US-dollar transactions and pressure to use SSP accounts.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: South Sudanese nationals are taxed on worldwide income, including income from entrepreneurial activities (Deloitte 2026). Individual rates for residents and non-residents run from 0% (up to SSP 20,000) to 20% (over SSP 90,000), and the rate for your bracket applies to the WHOLE taxable income, not just the excess (Deloitte 2026). The Financial Act 2024/2025 (assented 25 November 2024) changed business profit tax and other rates (KPMG). Rules for non-nationals' foreign income were not captured.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: There is no VAT in force yet. The revenue authority said VAT will be rolled out alongside the existing sales tax, with electronic invoicing (Eye Radio). Sales tax applies to manufacturers, importers and providers of specified services (such as hotel, restaurant, bar and telecommunication services) at rates from 1% to 20%. Registration is required for anyone who imports goods, produces goods or supplies specified services in South Sudan (Deloitte 2026). Freelance or professional services are not named among the specified services in Deloitte's summary.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: No data-protection law yet. The government said in December 2025 it would introduce its first Data Protection Bill in 2026. A Cybercrime and Abuse of Computer Bill 2025 had passed parliament and was awaiting assent.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
